title: docs: the navigationContributions section does not say a contributed entry's `order` sorts it among the target app's own entries
body:
domain:spec#1 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5mswnWm181XgYcCUag

Follow-up of #33234 (ruled C, no change; ruling record 6884379643), part (2), class a, docs gap.

**What the card's filer believed:** a module cannot place its contributed entry between two of the app's own entries, because "a contribution is appended after the target group's own items".

**What the code does (read on `main` by the seat, not run):**
- `SchemaRegistry.applyNavContributions` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` ~:10842) pushes each contribution's `items` into the target group's `children` (or the top level) as authored, `order` and all.
- The console sorts every level by `order` after the fold: `ui/packages/layout/src/navOrder.ts#byNavOrder`, used at the top level and in each group's children (`NavigationRenderer.tsx`) and by the mobile tab bar (`AppSchemaRenderer.tsx`). No `order` sorts as `0`; equal values keep authored (fold) order.
- So a contributed `{ ..., order: 25 }` lands between the app's `order: 20` and `order: 30` entries, in a group or at the top level. It only works if the app numbers its own entries; with none numbered, every entry is `0` and a contribution stays after the app's own items.

**Gap:** `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx`, the `navigationContributions` section (~:829-870), describes `group` and `priority` only. `priority` orders contributions among themselves; nothing says the item's own `order` places it among the host's entries, or that the host has to number its entries for that. The "Navigation items" table (~:297) says `order` sorts "within the same level" without saying that contributed entries take part.

**TO:**
1. One short paragraph (and one line in the example) in the contributions section: the merged items sort with the host's entries of that level by `order`; `priority` is only the merge order between contributions, the tie-break for equal `order`; give the "host must number its entries" consequence.
2. A pin, objectql side: a registry test that a contributed item keeps its `order` through `applyNavContributions` (group and top level), so the fold never re-numbers or drops it. The console sort is already pinned by `byNavOrder`'s tests; cite them in the docs paragraph's commit, do not duplicate them.

No rule change, no new key. `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none`; docs plus one test, `@objectstack/objectql` no bump unless a source line moves.

class: a · type: Docs · Grade: p3 (docs gap; a downstream filer misread it, product right) · domain: spec
